consensus_summary: Primary meaning is the divine presence and glory of God (Shekinah theophany) that simultaneously reveals and conceals Him, guides and protects, fills tabernacle/temple, and appears at Sinai, Transfiguration, Ascension and return; secondary/context-specific alternatives include eschatological judgment, cloud of witnesses (multitude), transience, empty promises (clouds without water), concealment, and rain/blessing.
book_summary: The vehicle of heaven (clouds as chariot) whose cargo is the word/doctrine (dropping as rain); encompasses the pillar that led Israel, the cloud that received Christ and returns Him, the transport of the caught-up saints, and the airborne multitude that is the cloud of witnesses; counterfeit is the cloud without water.
consensus_core_identification: divine presence and glory of God (theophanic Shekinah)
book_core_identification: vehicle/chariot of heaven carrying the word, for transport of Christ/saints and as airborne multitude of witnesses
boundary_disagreement: Book unifies the chariot, leading pillar, ascension/return/rapture clouds, and cloud of witnesses under one vehicle/multitude image (plus word-cargo and counterfeit), whereas consensus keeps presence/glory as primary and treats witnesses, empty clouds, and pure transport/eschatology as secondary or separate metaphors; book omits settled emphasis on glory-filling, concealment, and judgment-darkness.
material_contradiction: Consensus core identifies the cloud as God's manifest presence/glory; book replaces that central identification with vehicle of heaven whose cargo is the word, so the two primary claims cannot both be the settled core meaning of the same symbol.
rationale: Minimum cores differ: every consensus response settles on presence/glory (Shekinah) as the dominant theophanic referent attested across traditions and the listed primary texts, while the book never names presence or glory and instead installs the chariot/vehicle image (Ps 104:3) plus doctrine-as-rain cargo as the organizing identification, then folds the witnesses and counterfeit into it. Overlapping proof-texts do not erase the replacement of the central referent; extensions therefore show partial reclassification rather than simple narrowing or broadening of an intact core.
strongest_objection: Vehicle/chariot language already appears inside the consensus presence reading (Ps 104:3), and every concrete case the book lists is already a consensus primary or alternative, so the difference could be argued as mere emphasis (REFINED) rather than core replacement.
